You've been told hard inquiries can't be removed — and that's simply wrong

Unauthorized hard inquiries can absolutely be removed. Federal law gives you that right. Most people just don't know which laws apply, how to use them, or who actually specializes in doing this correctly.

Here is what most people never find out — the hard inquiries that don't belong on your report don't have to stay there for two years. You have federal rights. We know exactly how to use them.

There Is a Better Way. And It Was Built for Exactly This.

Robert Garcia founded Inquiry Removal in 2015 after living this problem firsthand. He walked into a dealership, told them not to send his application anywhere, and watched as his perfect credit took a 100-point hit from inquiries he never authorized. As a former senior credit analyst who spent years in the disputes department of a major financial institution, he knew those inquiries didn't belong there — and he knew which federal laws could remove them.

So he built the only company in the country that does one thing and one thing only: removes hard inquiries. Not collections. Not late payments. Not charge-offs. Just inquiries. That singular focus means our team knows the FCRA, FDCPA, FACTA, and Metro 2 compliance standards at a depth that generalist credit repair companies simply don't have — because for them, inquiries are one line item on a long checklist. For us, they are the entire job.

Many broad credit repair companies were built on monthly subscriptions. The longer you stay stuck, the more they earn. They need you in the problem. We operate on a single flat fee because we need you out of it. We fight alongside you against the dealerships that ignored your instructions, the identity thieves who opened lines of credit in your name, and the bureaus that keep verifying inquiries that were never authorized. When you win, we're done. That's how it should work.

The people who come to us aren't financially irresponsible. They're people who went car shopping and got ambushed. They're people whose information was stolen. They're people who applied online and had no idea their report would be sent to thirty different lenders. They deserve better than a monthly subscription that turns their problem into someone else's profit.

If we do not remove any hard inquiries from your credit report within 90 days of beginning service, you receive a full refund — no runaround, no finger-pointing, no fine print designed to keep your money.

We verify results before processing any refund, because that is the honest way to handle it. In nearly 11 years and over 1,123 clients, we have maintained a near-100% success rate. We tell you about the guarantee not because we expect to use it — but because you deserve to know it exists before you trust us with anything.

Individual results vary based on each client's specific credit report, inquiry type, and bureau response. Most clients see removals within 30 to 90 days.

Frequently Asked Questions About Hard Inquiry Removal

Will this actually work for my situation? +

Yes — if you have unauthorized, excessive, or fraudulent hard inquiries on your credit report, we can dispute them using federal law. We offer a completely free consultation specifically so you can see exactly what's removable and what your score improvement could look like before you spend anything. No two credit reports are identical, which is why we look at yours first.

Can you really remove hard inquiries — or just dispute them? +

We have permanently removed over 100,437 hard inquiries across Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion since 2015. We do this using the FCRA, FDCPA, FACTA, and Metro 2 compliance laws — not generic templates, not guesswork. Our near-100% success rate exists because we know which law applies to which type of inquiry and why. Disputing and removing are the same outcome when you know what you're doing.

How soon will I see results? +

Some clients see their first removals in as few as 14 days. Most see full results within 30 to 90 days. We are transparent about timelines from the very first conversation — we work as fast as the law allows because we know your goals are on a real schedule.

What if I've already tried another company and got nothing? +

We hear this regularly, and the answer is almost always the same: the company you worked with was a generalist. They treated inquiry removal as one item on a long checklist, using the same strategy they'd use for a collection or a late payment. Inquiry removal requires a completely different approach — specific federal laws applied to specific inquiry types, sent to specific bureaus in a specific way. That specialization is the only thing we do. It's why we succeed where others stall.
